component.name: Fretwork
component.summary: Play every track of a tab as its own stem

description.p: Fretwork is a tablature program for Linux that treats a score as a multitrack session. It reads Guitar Pro files, converts them to a format of its own, and renders each track through a separate synthesised instrument — so a track can be soloed, sent through its own amplifier simulation, and exported as an independent audio file.

That last part is the reason the program exists. Linux already has a tablature editor. What it has not had is a tablature program that gives you one synth per track, per-track LV2 effects, and real stems out the other end.

ul.li: Open a Guitar Pro file and draw the tablature, with the bar being played lit up as it goes
Give every track its own synthesiser, so solo and mute take effect while it plays
Let you edit — fret entry, rhythm, bars, selection, copy and paste, undo, transposition, tuning and capo
Export one audio file per track, wet or dry, or a backing track with a part removed
Tune your instrument from the audio input

description.p: Where a score asks for something Fretwork cannot honestly play, it says so rather than approximating it. The list of what those things are is in the documentation, and it is short and getting shorter.
"Guitar Pro" is a trademark of Arobas Music. Fretwork is not affiliated with them, not derived from their software, and ships none of their soundbanks or artwork.

description.p: First release. A tablature editor and player with per-track synthesis and stem export. Per-track LV2 chains and SFZ sampling are present and experimental.
